findings.summary: As attached, the rendered figure carries no text at all, so a reader sees five blank boxes, five blank boxes' arrows and three unlabelled dots. The evidence fragment's alt text and caption promise named content ('a single gate', 'the three arms', the readers each answers), and none of it appears in the PNG: no gate label, no box label, no arm label, no reader name, no legend word. A diagram whose every box is empty communicates neither the source-precedence rule nor which of the five boxes is the gate and which three are the measured arms, so the figure cannot be read at all. This is a defect of the delivered render, not of the drawing's numbers; the artefact a reader receives here has no glyphs (verified: 143 near-black pixels on the whole canvas, zero non-white pixels inside all five box interiors, and the alpha channel bottoms out at 128 with no fully transparent text layer).

note: Judged only from the attached PNG named in this review, opened with the Read tool and then measured pixel by pixel; no SVG was opened, read, searched or rendered. The attached PNG is a 1399x720 RGBA raster (the figure's 14 x 7.2 in canvas at 100 dpi) and is the only image this review inspected. Read-only review: no file was edited, created, moved, deleted or redrawn, including the figure, its SVG and its caption; the only files written are the two declared review records. The caption at docs/evidence/fragments/history-persists-as-detail-washes-out/ledger-reads-the-store-s22.html ('One gate decides the source for every reader. The three arms beneath it are the measured runs in the second table.') was read only to check whether it merely repeats a title; it does not, it adds the reading instruction the figure is meant to need, so no caption finding is recorded. Because the PNG shows no labels at all, the caption cannot rescue the figure: nothing the caption names is visible in the image it sits under.

rubric_items.contrast: States defect. There is no text to clear contrast against anything, so no label in this image can be read at all; the visible ink (grey #999999 and #929292 outlines, blue #2f6db3 arrows) reads clearly against white, which is why the missing labels are a text problem rather than a colour problem.
rubric_items.data_ink: Defect. The ink is five empty outlines, five arrows and three unlabelled dots. The one fact the figure exists to carry, that a single gate decides the source for every reader and that three measured arms sit beneath it, is carried by no visible mark: the caption beneath promises 'one gate' and 'the three arms', and no box in the image says which is which.
rubric_items.decoration: Passes. No gradient, no background fill, no shadow, no frame and no styled theme: the boxes are white with a thin grey outline (the canvas holds 2,547 px of #999999 and 2,873 px of #929292) and the highlighted path is a single clean blue (#2f6db3, 3,335 px). Nothing decorative competes with the drawing; the defect is missing text, not added ornament.
rubric_items.label_collision: States defect. No label is drawn, so no label is clipped, overlapping another label, or overlapping the data; the absence is recorded here so this item is not read as a pass, and an empty canvas cannot be called collision-free in any useful sense.
rubric_items.legibility: Fails. The 1399x720 PNG draws five rounded boxes and five connector arrows, and no text anywhere: every box interior is pure white (0 non-white pixels in 22,066; 15,281; 32,319; 32,319 and 90,398 interior pixels across the five boxes), and the whole canvas carries only 143 near-black pixels, fewer than one glyph. The three marks at the bottom (an 8 px dot at x 48-55, y 643-651 and two at x 635-643, y 643-651 and y 679-687) are drawn with no adjacent text. A reader is given five unlabelled boxes and cannot tell which is the gate, which is the source of the second table, which arm was measured, or what any connector means.
rubric_items.table_form: Passes. The image depicts a source-precedence flow, a gate and the routes beneath it; the nine readers and what each answers are set out in a real table in the same evidence fragment, and the figure is not a table drawn as boxes.
